decisions.quote: Despite these limitations, we were able to replicate the original report. Our data also indicate that the gene-based association of these loss-of-function variants is independent of the GWAS variant, and that the aggregate effect of these variants is larger than that of the common variant alone.
decisions.reason: Under Rule 1 of the codebook, an explicit overall verdict on the replication as a whole outweighs individual contrasts. Although single-variant tests did not reach statistical significance in the European-American sample (just as Steinberg et al. [1] themselves failed to replicate single variants in their non-Icelandic European replication cohort and only replicated the association at the gene level), the authors explicitly conclude in the Abstract Conclusions, Results and discussion ('Despite these limitations, we were able to replicate the original report'), and Conclusions ('In summary, our study replicates the association of ABCA7 loss-of-function variants with AD risk') that they replicated the original report.

decisions.quote: Additionally, none of these loss-of-function variants were in linkage disequilibrium (LD) with the ABCA7 common variant identified by GWAS [ 2 ], suggesting that there are multiple and independent mechanisms throughout the ABCA7 region that increase risk for AD. Based on these results, we tried to replicate the association of the ABCA7 loss-of-function variants in a large cohort of European–Americans.
decisions.reason: Lambert et al. (2013) [2] is cited only once in the Introduction as background identifying the previously reported GWAS common variant (rs4147929). The paper explicitly identifies Steinberg et al. [1] as 'the original study' and genotypes rs4147929 as a power check and to confirm Steinberg et al.'s finding that the ABCA7 loss-of-function variants are independent of (not in LD with) the common GWAS signal, rather than as an independent target replication of Lambert et al. [2].
